rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is secretly speaking in repeated words; the whispering sound of jewelry is also called waswas.
rows.anchor: وسوس إذا تكلم كلاما خفيا يكرره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is intransitive, like a woman ululating and a wolf howling; the passive-derived adjective is pronounced with kasra, not fatha.
rows.anchor: وهو فعل غيرمتعد كقولنا : ولولوت المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mوسوس له means whispering for someone's sake, while موسوس إليه means casting the whisper to its recipient.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وسوس له فعل الوسوسة لأجله ووسوس إليه ألقاها إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Satan whispered upward from earth to heaven and the Garden using the superior power God gave him.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : كان يوسوس من الأرض إلى السماء وإلى الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani says Adam and Iblis were both in the Garden, which was one of the gardens of earth.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصفهاني : بل كان آدم وإبليس في الجنة

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some tell the story that Iblis entered a snake and the snake entered the Garden; al-Razi calls it flimsy.
rows.anchor: والذي يقوله بعض الناس من أن إبليس دخل في جوف الحية ودخلت الحية في الجنة فتلك القصة الركيكة مشهورة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say Adam and Eve approached the Garden gate while Iblis stood outside, close enough to whisper.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إن آدم وحواء ربما قربا من باب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Adam knew Iblis was his enemy, repeated approaches and persistent deception could eventually affect him.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يقال إن إبليس لقي آدم مرارا كثيرة ورغبه في أكل الشجرة بطرق كثيرة فلأجل المواظبة والمداومة على هذا التمويه أثر كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وسوس لهما, the particle له means Satan performed the whispering for their sake.
rows.anchor: السؤال الثالث : لم قال : { فوسوس لهما الشيطان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes the lām as consequence: Satan intended sin, not exposure, and did not know eating would uncover their nakedness; compare 28:8.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه لام العاقبة كما في قوله : { فالتقطه ءال فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose and exposure metaphorically means loss of honor and rank, which was Satan's aim.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل بدو العورة كناية عن سقوط الحرمة وزوال الجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan may have known from the Preserved Tablet or angels that eating would expose them, and intended that harmful loss of honor.
rows.anchor: لعله رأى في اللوح المحفوظ أو سمع من بعض الملائكة أنه إذا أكل من الشجرة بدت عورته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports Ibn Abbas reading ملكين and explaining they aspired to become angels; Satan tempted them through angelhood, as 20:120 says.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : كان ابن عباس يقرأ ملكين ويقول : ما طمعا في أن يكونا ملكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls that answer weak: it cannot imply the transmitted canonical reading is invalid, since that reading is mutawatir.
rows.anchor: وأقول هذا الجواب أيضا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the canonical reading remains valid, the difficulty returns: the inducement still made them hope eating would make them angels.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني : فعلى هذا التقدير الإشكال باق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve already had no higher honor to gain: angels prostrated to Adam, and they could dwell and eat freely in the Garden.
rows.anchor: ولا مزيد في الملك على هذه الدرجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not show angels outrank prophethood if the event occurred before Adam's prophethood, since he was not yet a prophet.
rows.anchor: إذا قلنا إن هذه الواقعة كانت قبل النبوة لم يدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the event was during prophethood, Adam may have wanted angelic strength, a luminous nature, or residence at the Throne and Kursi, not a higher rank.
rows.anchor: فلعل آدم عليه السلام رغب في أن يصير من الملائكة في القدرة والقوة والشدة أو في خلقة الذات بأن يصير جوهرا نورانيا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd asked al-Hasan whether Adam and Eve believed Iblis when he promised angelhood or immortality and swore he was sincere.
rows.anchor: نقل أن عمرو بن عبيد قال للحسن في قوله : إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan answered, 'God forbid'; if they had believed Iblis, they would have become disbelievers.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن معاذ الله لو صدقاه لكانا من الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument for calling belief in Iblis disbelief is that accepting immortality would deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: ذكروا في تقرير ذلك التكفير أنه عليه السلام لو صدق إبليس في الخلود لكان ذلك يوجب إنكار البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi counters that khulud can mean a very long stay rather than endless duration, removing the argument for disbelief.
rows.anchor: الخلود محمول على طول المكث لا على الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if khulud means eternity, Adam could suppose he might remain forever because knowledge of mortality requires revelation, which may not yet have come.
rows.anchor: فلعله تعالى ما بين في وقت آدم عليه السلام أنه يميت الخلق

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The careful scholars deny that Adam and Eve certainly or even probably assented to Satan's claim.
rows.anchor: أن المحققين أنكروا حصول هذا التصديق قطعا وظنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says they ate because desire overwhelmed them, not because they believed or suspected Satan; people may pursue desire without believing another's pitch.
rows.anchor: بل الصواب أنهما إنما أقدما على الأكل لغلبة الشهوة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the inducement offered angelhood and immortality together, since their combination made temptation stronger.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الترغيب كان في مجموع الأمرين

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others take the wording literally as a choice between becoming angels or immortals.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بل هو على ظاهره على طريقة التخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāsamah is reciprocal oath-taking: one swears to another and the other to him; qāsamtu means entering an oath pact, taqāsamū means swearing together.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : المقاسمة أن تقسم لصاحبك ويقسم لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi links the reciprocal oath term to the similar wording in 27:49.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { تقاسموا بالله لنبيتنه وأهله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to justice follows the account of God forbidding indecency and shows that God commands equity.
rows.anchor: لما بين أمر الأمر بالفحشاء بين تعالى أنه يأمر بالقسط والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing suggests justice is good in itself because of qualities belonging to it, and God commands it on that basis; al-Razi refers to his prior answer on intrinsic goodness.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل أيضا على أن الحسن إنما يحسن لوجوه عائدة إليه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata and al-Suddi explain qist as justice and what reason plainly recognizes as good and correct.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء ، والسدي { بالقسط } بالعدل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says qist means the testimony that there is no deity but God, citing 3:18 as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هو قول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi identifies the first command as the shahada, encompassing knowledge of God's essence, acts, rulings, and oneness.
rows.anchor: وهو يشتمل على معرفة الله تعالى بذاته وأفعاله وأحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To coordinate the command with the preceding statement, supply another 'say': 'Say: My Lord commands justice, and say: establish your faces...'.
rows.anchor: التقدير : قل أمر ربي بالقسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among readings of establishing one's face, al-Razi prefers facing the qibla, since sincerity is stated afterward.
rows.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول ، لأن الإخلاص مذكور من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects interpreting the phrase as sincerity because the next command already says to call on God sincerely, making that reading repetitious and incoherent.
rows.anchor: ولو حملناه على معنى الإخلاص ، صار كأنه قال : وأخلصوا عند كل مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although sincerity might attach only to supplication, the phrase can apply to both commands and should not be restricted, especially since religion covers all acts of devotion.
rows.anchor: لما أمكن رجوعه إليهما جميعا ، لم يجز قصره على أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase could refer to prayer time or place; the place-based reading is an alternative to al-Razi's preferred time-based reading.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في أن المراد منه زمان الصلاة أو مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi prefers prayer time: believers should face the Kaaba wherever they pray rather than privilege particular locations.
rows.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول ، لأنه الموضع الذي يمكن فيه إقامة الوجه للقبلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to pray at any mosque where one is when prayer time arrives, rather than insisting on one's clan's mosque.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : المراد إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد فصلوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the verse requires facing at every mosque but does not establish a prohibition on leaving one mosque for another.
rows.anchor: لأن لفظ الآية يدل على وجوب إقامة الوجه في كل مسجد ، ولا يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi takes calling on God sincerely as the acts of prayer: prayer literally means supplication, and its noblest parts are supplication and remembrance.
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن المراد به أعمال الصلاة ، وسماها دعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requirement to worship God sincerely parallels 98:5.
rows.anchor: ونطيره قوله تعالى : { وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people return as God began them: believers are raised believers and unbelievers unbelievers, according to the happiness or misery for which they were created and acted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { كما بدأكم } خلقكم مؤمنا أو كافرا

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say that just as God created people from nothing in this world, He will resurrect them alive.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن ومجاهد : { كما بدأكم } خلقكم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supporters of Ibn Abbas cite the next verse's division into a guided party and a party bound for error as explaining this return.
rows.anchor: احتجوا على صحته بأنه تعالى ذكر عقيبه قوله : { فريقا هدى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi objects that nobody says God first made us believers or unbelievers, since faith and unbelief must arise later.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا القول باطل ، لأن أحدا لا يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls the objection weak: 'beginning' can mean beginning in faith or unbelief, happiness or misery, and the same state holds at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا السؤال ضعيف ، لأن جوابه أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage orders the shahada, then prayer, and says their benefit appears in the afterlife, as in God's instructions to Moses in 20:14–15.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أن الفائدة في الإتيان بهذه الأعمال ، إنما تظهر في الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school cites this as evidence that God is the source of guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن الهدى والضلال من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites interpret guidance as directing people to Paradise and reward, and error as punishment and exclusion from reward.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : المراد فريقا هدى إلى الجنة والثواب

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues people deserve punishment, not being led astray from religion; otherwise prophets could be ordered to mislead them, undermining trust in prophecy.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : لأن هذا هو الذي يحق عليهم دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Mu'tazilite reading because هدَى is past tense, while their interpretation makes it future guidance to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { فريقا هدى } إشارة إلى الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues guidance and error are from God by conclusive rational proofs; even a divine decree makes another outcome impossible, since otherwise it would be false.
rows.anchor: لأنا بينا بالدلائل العقلية القاطعة أن الهدى والضلال ليسا إلا من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God decrees guidance or error, an opposite act cannot issue from the person, because that would entail a false divine judgment; thus the Mu'tazilite position fails.
rows.anchor: لما حصل هذا الحكم امتنع من العبد صدور غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative فَرِيقًا is governed by an omitted verb explained by what follows, as if the verse said 'He abandoned a party'.
rows.anchor: انتصاب قوله : { وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their error became due because they adopted satans as patrons, accepted their summons, and failed to distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: أنهم اتخذوا الشياطين أولياء من دون الله فقبلوا ما دعوهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi reconciles divine creation with this account: ability together with motive necessitates action, and their motive was taking Satan as patron.
rows.anchor: عندنا مجموع القدرة ، والداعي يوجب الفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes 'they suppose themselves guided' as what Amr ibn Luhay explained to them; al-Razi calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد ما بين لهم عمرو بن لحي ، وهذا بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording applies generally: anyone who institutes a false practice deserves blame and punishment whether or not they think it right; conjecture cannot establish religion, which requires certainty.
rows.anchor: بل هو محمول على عمومه ، فكل من شرع في باطل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school uses 'best of the openers' to show God creates faith in a servant; if the servant created faith, that servant would be the best opener, contradicting the verse.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذا اللفظ على أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is the noblest created thing; even if fatḥ means disclosure and clarification, faith fits that description, reinforcing that God is the best opener.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيمان أشرف المحدثات ، ولو فسرنا لفتح بالكشف والتبيين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the chiefs called Shuayb's followers losers in religion.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فقال بعضهم : خاسرون في الدين

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say they meant worldly losers, because following Shuayb would stop them taking extra wealth from people.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : خاسرون في الدنيا ، لأنه يمنعكم من أخذ الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people completed their corruption by going astray themselves and leading others astray, so they deserved destruction.
rows.anchor: وعند هذا المقال كمل حالهم في الضلال أولا وفي الإضلال ثانيا ، فاستحقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajfa was a violent deadly earthquake; together with the earlier severe punishment, it made their destruction more complete.
rows.anchor: وهي الزلزلة الشديدة المهلكة ، فإذا انضاف إليها الجزاء الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their home means their dwellings, and they lay motionless and lifeless.
rows.anchor: فأصبحوا في دارهم } أي في مساكنهم { جاثمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says ghani means that people stayed a long time in their home; maghna refers to a dwelling.
rows.anchor: يقال غني القوم في دارهم إذا طال مقامهم فيها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line about their having lived amid the best life witnesses the sense 'they dwelled there'.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة … في ظل ملك ثابت الأوتاد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains it as 'as if they had not lived there in comfort'; ghaniya means becoming self-sufficient, from richness opposed to poverty.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : كأن لم يغنوا فيها ، كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, God likens the deniers to people who had never been in those dwellings, as a poet's lines illustrate.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يكن بين الحجون إلى الصفا … أنيس ولم يسمر بمكة سامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That only Shuayb's deniers were punished shows the event came from a freely acting creator, not the stars or nature, which would also affect his followers.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك العذاب إنما حدث بتخليق فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The selective punishment shows its cause knows every particular and can distinguish obedient people from disobedient ones.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن ذلك الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishing some people but not others in the same town is a great miracle proving Shuayb's truth.
rows.anchor: يدل على المعجز العظيم في حق شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'those who denied Shuayb' intensifies their humiliation and the dreadful punishment they deserved; Arabs repeat for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وإنما كرر قوله : { الذين كذبوا شعيبا } لتعظيم المذلة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated clause also reverses the chiefs' claim: those who refused to follow Shuayb were the actual losers.
rows.anchor: لما قالوا : { لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون } بين تعالى أن الذين لم يتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differed on whether Shuayb turned away before or after punishment; al-Kalbi says he left their midst, since a prophet's people are not punished until he departs.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أنه تولى بعد نزول العذاب بهم أو قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asā means intense grief; al-Ajjaj's poetic line about eyes overflowing from grief witnesses the meaning.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج : وانحلبت عيناه من فرط الأسى …

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes Shuayb's words as real grief: he had hoped a large familiar community would believe, but reminds himself they brought destruction on themselves.
rows.anchor: أنه اشتد حزنه على قومه ، لأنهم كانوا كثيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means he delivered the message, counseled and warned them; since they rejected it, they did not deserve grief.
rows.anchor: لقد أعذرت إليكم في الإبلاغ والنصيحة والتحذير مما حل بكم ، فلم تسمعوا قولي

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that Yahya ibn Waththab read فكيف with kasra on the hamza.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب { فكيف } بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This phrase indicates that the earlier promise in 7:167 concerned the whole Jewish people, whom God dispersed widely.
rows.anchor: قوله : { ليبعثن عليهم } ( الأعراف : 167 ) المراد جملة اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispersion means scarcely any inhabited country lacks a Jewish community; this is the usual state of affairs.
rows.anchor: وظاهر ذلك أنه لا أرض مسكونة إلا ومنهم فيها أمة ، وهذا هو الغالب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the righteous as people of Moses's time, when a community guided by truth existed among them.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد القوم الذين كانوا في زمن موسى عليه السلام لأنه كان فيهم أمة يهدون بالحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the righteous as those who lived to meet the Prophet Muhammad and believed him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد : يريد الذين أدركوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وآمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people 'below that' are those who remained Jewish, as distinct from the righteous group.
rows.anchor: أي ومنهم قوم دون ذلك ، والمراد من أقام على اليهودية

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objection proposes this means people who were righteous but less righteous than the first group, closer to the surface wording.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : لم لا يجوز أن يكون قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that 'so that they might return' in 7:169 shows this means people who persisted in Judaism and left righteousness.
rows.anchor: قلنا : أن قوله بعد ذلك : { لعلهم يرجعون } يدل على أن المراد بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good things are blessings, fertility, and health; bad things are famine and hardships.
rows.anchor: وهي النعم والخصب والعافية ، والسيئات هي الجدب والشدائد

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meanings say prosperity and adversity prompt obedience: blessings encourage it and afflictions warn through fear.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : وكل واحد من الحسنات والسيئات يدعو إلى الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hoped-for return means repentance.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { يرجعون } يريد كي يتوبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot help worshippers or defend themselves against the disobedient; a deity must be able to benefit and repel harm, which idols cannot do.
rows.anchor: يريد أن الأصنام لا تنصر من أطاعها ولا تنتصر ممن عصاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot protect themselves from harm; for example, they cannot resist someone who tries to break them.
rows.anchor: أي ولا يدفعون عن أنفسهم مكروها فإن من أراد كسرهم لم يقدروا على دفعه

words: وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَى لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing idols have no power, the verse shows they have no knowledge: they do not follow guidance or distinguish being addressed from being ignored.
rows.anchor: لما أثبت بالآية المتقدمة أنه لا قدرة لهذه الأصنام على أمر من الأمور ، بين بهذه الآية

words: سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement resembles 2:6, though there the warning clause is coordinated with another verbal clause, while here a verbal clause is paired with a nominal clause.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله : { سواء عليهم ءأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here a verbal sentence is coordinated with a nominal one; verbs suggest renewal, while nominal sentences suggest constancy and continuity.
rows.anchor: وتلك الفائدة هي أن صيغة الفعل مشعرة بالتجدد والحدوث حالا بعد حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists called idols in urgent troubles and stayed silent otherwise; neither calling nor continued silence makes a difference to idols.
rows.anchor: إن هؤلاء المشركين كانوا إذا وقعوا في مهم وفي معضلة تضرعوا إلى تلك الأصنام ، وإذا لم تحدث تلك الواقعة بقوا ساكتين صامتين

words: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling idols servants like worshippers raises the question how this applies to inanimate objects; al-Razi begins by answering that the wording addresses idolaters' beliefs.
rows.anchor: وفيه سؤال : وهو أنه كيف يحسن وصفها بأنها عباد مع أنها جمادات ؟ وجوابه من وجوه : الأول

words: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because idolaters claim idols benefit and harm, the verse addresses them as if they believe idols intelligent; masculine الذين and فليستجيبوا match that presumed belief.
rows.anchor: ادعوا أنها تضر وتنفع ، وجب أن يعتقدوا فيها كونها عاقلة فاهمة
